title: The state quartet on every route and data-bearing component
iWant: considered screens when things are empty, loading, or broken
soThat: the application never looks abandoned at exactly the wrong moment

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every data-bearing route renders designed loading, empty, error, and success states; a state matrix over the route inventory has no unspecified applicable cell.
acceptanceCriteria.when: each applicable state is induced per route
acceptanceCriteria.then: every applicable cell renders a designed state

acceptanceCriteria.description: Loading states use skeletons wherever the incoming content shape is known; spinners appear only for indeterminate operations per spa-US-1112.
acceptanceCriteria.then: known shapes use skeletons; spinner use is justified

acceptanceCriteria.description: Empty states are per-context, naming the specific absent content and its filling action; a single generic empty component text is not reused verbatim across unrelated routes.
acceptanceCriteria.when: copy and action are compared across routes
acceptanceCriteria.then: each names its own content and action

acceptanceCriteria.description: Error states distinguish user-fixable failures from system failures and offer retry on transient failures (network, 5xx); not on user-fixable 4xx.
Success states after mutations confirm the outcome visibly (toast or inline confirmation per the journey spec) and reflect the new data without manual refresh.
acceptanceCriteria.then: confirmation renders and affected views show the new data

acceptanceCriteria.description: State transitions never flash intermediate wrong states: loading does not flicker for cached data, and empty never renders while data is still loading.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a route with cached data and a route loading slowly
acceptanceCriteria.then: no wrong-state flash occurs in either
